paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD finishes what He starts. Babylon looked untouchable, with towers up, walls built and gods on every corner. But the LORD says, "Babylon is captured," and He says it before it happens (Jeremiah 50:2). When He announces the end of a power that big, the baker can trust Him with the powers that feel too big in their own life.

Now look at who He's talking about. His people were "lost sheep," and the ones who found them devoured them and called themselves not guilty (Jeremiah 50:6-7). The LORD doesn't pretend they weren't scattered, and He doesn't let the ones who crushed them walk off with a clean note on the windshield. He says to Babylon, "as she has done, do the same to her" (Jeremiah 50:15). Friend, He sees what was done to His people, and He answers it.

And then comes the best part, so hang onto it. He says, "I will return Israel to his pasture," and a search for their guilt will find none, "for I will forgive the remnant I preserve" (Jeremiah 50:19-20). They don't earn the trip home. He brings them, and He forgives them. I know a little about being carried out of a dark place I couldn't climb out of myself, and I can tell you it's the sweetest ride there is. So whenever you feel lost or scattered, baker, remember who the Shepherd is, and let Him bring you home.
